title: The Service Charge on Catering Produced Out of a Client's Own Cafe Kitchen
content:
The service charge raised on a catering order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement answers the brigade that served the order, and what the client holds under the Workplace Cafe Management Program at the agreement's delivery site therefore decides the percentage.

**Where the client holds a cafe contract at the agreement's delivery site that stands active and whose service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen** — no service charge is raised, the client's own cafe brigade having served the order.

**Where the client holds a cafe contract at that site that stands active and whose service model does not permit catering to be ordered out of that kitchen** — the service charge is half, that is 0.5 or 50 per cent, of the percentage printed against the catering service level, the cafe team having set down what the district kitchen produced.

**Where the client holds no cafe contract at that site, or holds one that does not stand active** — the service charge is the whole percentage printed against the catering service level.

### The records this is read from

The site tested is the delivery site written on the Corporate Catering Service Agreement. Against that site the client's Workplace Cafe Management Program contract is read for two things: whether the contract stands active, and whether catering may be ordered out of that cafe kitchen under the service model recorded on it.

| Cafe contract at the agreement's delivery site | Catering may be ordered out of that cafe kitchen | Percentage of the printed service charge that is raised |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stands active | yes | none |
| Stands active | no | half, that is 0.5 or 50 per cent |
| Does not stand active | either way | the whole percentage |
| No such contract | — | the whole percentage |

The first two rows are written for a contract that stands active at that site; a contract in any other standing leaves the order on the whole percentage, whatever its service model permits.

### Illustration on hypothetical figures

On a hypothetical order whose catering service level is printed with a service charge of 14.0 per cent and whose discounted food and beverage value is 1000.00 USD: where the client's cafe contract at that site stands active and catering may be ordered out of that kitchen under its service model, no service charge is raised; where that contract stands active but catering may not be ordered out of that kitchen, the percentage raised is 7.0 per cent, giving 70.00 USD; where the client holds no cafe contract at that site, the percentage raised is 14.0 per cent, giving 140.00 USD.
